description: Work a story with no test-first step: do the change, verify it against the acceptance criteria, commit, close out.

story.description: the story bead this formula works

steps.title: Verify
steps.description: Run whatever {{story}}'s acceptance criteria say to check, and confirm it passes.

steps.title: Commit
steps.description: Commit the change for {{story}} in small, plainly described commits, with no AI attribution lines.

steps.title: Closing comment
steps.description: Comment on {{story}} with what was done, what was verified and how, and anything left undone. Before that section, when the story changes something the Governor can see, add a section headed exactly 'HOW TO CHECK IT, for the Governor': at most six plain numbered steps with the exact on-screen labels and what right looks like; otherwise write the single line 'Internal: nothing for the Governor to look at'. Also give one line, 'What's new: New: <one plain sentence the Governor would understand, no file names>' or 'What's new: Fixed: <one plain sentence, no file names>', or 'What's new: none' for a change he cannot see (tests, docs, internal): mw next writes it into the app's changelog when the rig keeps one. END the closing comment with a section headed exactly 'For the rig memory:' holding at most two typed facts that a later Builder on this rig would have been saved real time by, one per line, each in one of these forms: 'gotcha [subject]: <sentence>', 'decision [subject]: <sentence>', 'supersede <slug>: <sentence>', 'retire <slug>: <reason>', 'recheck <slug>: <why>' (a slug names a fact the rig memory already holds), or the single word 'nothing'. mw next passes each line to the Mayor as the mw memory command that places it, and flags a line it cannot read. The Builder does NOT edit the rig memory file: the Mayor places what he keeps.
